gloss: to exterminate; to slay; to get rid of

definitions.gloss: to exterminate; to slay; to get rid of
definitions.explanation: To defeat and eliminate monsters, pests, villains, or other undesirable things. Used both in folklore and legends (slaying demons) and in everyday life (getting rid of pests).

examples.japanese: {台所|だいどころ}のゴキブリを{退治|たいじ}した。
examples.english: I got rid of the cockroach in the kitchen.

examples.japanese: {桃太郎|ももたろう}は{犬|いぬ}と{猿|さる}ときじを{連|つ}れて、{鬼|おに}ヶ{島|しま}の{鬼|おに}を{退治|たいじ}しに{行|い}った。
examples.english: Momotaro took a dog, a monkey, and a pheasant with him and went to Onigashima to slay the demons.

notes:
A word deeply rooted in Japanese folklore, where heroes slay monsters and demons. In everyday use, commonly applied to getting rid of household pests. Has a somewhat dramatic or heroic tone even in mundane contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鬼|おに}{退治|たいじ}: demon slaying
- {害虫|がいちゅう}{退治|たいじ}: pest extermination
- ゴキブリ{退治|たいじ}: cockroach extermination
- {悪者|わるもの}を{退治|たいじ}する: to defeat the villain

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many famous Japanese folktales center on {退治|たいじ}: {桃太郎|ももたろう}の{鬼|おに}{退治|たいじ} (Momotaro's demon slaying), {大江山|おおえやま}の{酒呑童子|しゅてんどうじ}{退治|たいじ} (slaying Shuten-doji), and {蜘蛛|くも}{退治|たいじ} (spider slaying) are among the most well-known.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {駆除|くじょ}する: to exterminate (pests) — more technical and practical, used by pest control professionals, while {退治|たいじ} has a more narrative or dramatic quality
- {倒|たお}す: to defeat — broader meaning of defeating an opponent, without the specific "eliminate the threat" nuance of {退治|たいじ}
